issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) specifies that Animal's constructor, getName(), and setName() should have protected visibility (UML uses '#' and the text explicitly instructs protected getter/setter). The solution implementation declares Animal(String) constructor and the getName()/setName() methods as public. This visibility mismatch between the specification and the provided solution can confuse students about the intended access level and may cause tests or grading checks that expect protected members to fail or be misleading.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the specification: change Animal's constructor and the getName()/setName() methods to protected in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java so they match the UML and the textual instruction. Alternatively, if public visibility was intended, update the problem statement/UML to state that the constructor and getter/setter are public to avoid confusion.
